$comment: Authored voice direction for recorded performances. `text` must equal the phrase's authored text exactly (it is the caption). `input` is what the TTS model receives: the same words, shaped by delivery tags, ellipses and emphasis — never added words. `scene` is unspoken context (the other person's line before/after, or a line of narration) that shapes how the words are said; it is sent as previous_text/next_text, is never heard, and is not billed. `interpretation` names the reading of the line; `context` weights the EmotionalField values that make this performance the right one; `fits` lists the voice styles it can stand in for. `retired` keeps an older take on disk and in the ledger but out of the room. Generation status, costs and review decisions live in scripts/dialogue-ledger.json, never here. `levelDb` is the take's level relative to the others (playback only half-normalises recordings, so a whispered take stays quieter than a raised voice). `audition` marks an alternative reading kept for listening: like a retired take, it reaches the room only if someone approves it.

intimate.identity: A young adult, gentle, imperfect, slightly hesitant. Speaks as if to one specific person at close range: warmth, uncertainty, guarded affection.

restrained.identity: A grounded, ordinary adult. Keeps composure; emotion gets through anyway. Never theatrical, never cold for effect.

warm.identity: Expressive and spontaneous, relaxed, laughs easily. Affectionate familiarity; happy memories told without sentiment.

distant.identity: Quiet and introspective, as if remembering a conversation from years ago. Emotionally ambiguous rather than sad.

young.library: Will (ElevenLabs default voice; a young adult voice, not a child)
young.identity: Youthful vulnerability: uncertainty, curiosity, the fragile feeling of being misunderstood. A synthetic stock voice; it imitates no real person.

sarah.identity: A young woman, soft-spoken but direct. Shy warmth, uncertainty she doesn't hide.

liam.identity: A young man. Quick to laugh, quick to bristle; embarrassed by his own feelings.

matilda.identity: A woman in middle age. Warm, tired, has carried other people for a long time.

bill.identity: An older man. Unhurried; the past is very near to him.

performances.input: [softly] I wanted you to stay.
performances.direction: Close and warm, not sad. Finally said out loud, to the one person it was for.

performances.input: I wanted you to stay.
performances.direction: Difficult to admit. Even and held back; the last word lands flatter than intended.

performances.input: [thoughtfully] I wanted you to stay.
performances.direction: Recalling something said years ago, not saying it now. Neither bitter nor resolved.

performances.input: [nervously] Please don't come any closer.
performances.direction: Not a threat. A request from someone who wants the opposite and is embarrassed by it.

performances.input: Please don't come any closer.
performances.direction: Level and polite. The politeness is the wall.

performances.input: [softly] I was afraid you'd leave.
performances.direction: Quietly confessional. A slight hesitation before 'leave'. No crying, no theatrical sadness: admitting something long concealed.

performances.input: I was afraid you'd leave.
performances.direction: Remembered rather than felt; almost wry about how afraid they were.

performances.text: If I come closer, will you stay?
performances.input: [hesitant] If I come closer, will you stay?
performances.direction: A real question, asked carefully, half expecting the wrong answer.

performances.input: [frustrated] Why didn't you understand?
performances.direction: Frustration under control, not shouting. Tired of having asked.

performances.input: [quietly] Why didn't you understand?
performances.direction: Not an accusation. Genuinely asking, years too late.

performances.input: I love you. Go away.
performances.direction: Both sentences meant. Tired. No anger on 'go away'.

performances.input: [laughs softly] I love you. Go away.
performances.direction: Affectionate, half-joking, the way you push someone off the sofa.

performances.input: I still say 'we' by accident.
performances.direction: Matter-of-fact, almost amused at oneself; the smallest catch on 'accident'.

performances.text: You made me laugh so hard I couldn't breathe.
performances.input: [laughing] You made me laugh so hard I couldn't breathe.
performances.direction: A genuinely happy memory, laughing a little in the telling, not performing it.

performances.text: You understood me once, completely, for about a minute.
performances.input: You understood me once, completely, for about a minute.
performances.direction: Fond and wry. 'About a minute' is both the joke and the wound.

performances.input: [amused] You've got crumbs on you.
performances.direction: Ordinary, close, teasing; leaning in to brush them off.

performances.input: Do you remember me?
performances.direction: Small and hopeful, ready for the answer to be no.

performances.input: I'm glad you came.
performances.direction: Simple. Shy relief. Not a greeting card.

performances.input: [quietly] I'm still here.
performances.direction: Not spooky. Reassuring, and a little surprised to be saying it.

performances.input: I'm not going anywhere.
performances.direction: Steady and plain. It could be a promise or it could be resignation.

performances.text: Don't go yet, this bit's good.
performances.input: Don't go yet, this bit's good.
performances.direction: Casual, eyes still on the screen, a hand on someone's arm.

performances.text: There's nothing wrong with being alone.
performances.input: There's nothing wrong with being alone.
performances.direction: Said to oneself, not preached. Almost indifferent.

performances.text: I'm sorry I was like that.
performances.input: [embarrassed] I'm sorry I was like that.
performances.direction: Awkward. A breath of a laugh at oneself before the apology.

performances.text: I think I was happy then.
performances.input: I think I was happy then.
performances.direction: Surprised by the thought. The 'I think' is real doubt, not modesty.

performances.input: I remember your laugh.
performances.direction: Unguarded, a small smile in it. Remembering the sound, not the loss.

performances.input: Was it me?
performances.direction: Almost under the breath. Asking oneself as much as anyone.

performances.input: [holding back tears] I wanted you… [voice cracking] to stay.
performances.interpretation: A vulnerable, nearly breaking admission.
performances.direction: Adopted from the voice lab (lab-stay-d-v4-scene-prose). Admitting it costs her; the voice goes on the last words.

scene.before: He already had his coat on. She had told him it was fine, that she understood. It was not fine. At the door she finally said it, and her voice gave way halfway through:

performances.input: [frustrated, voice rising] I WANTED you to stay. [scoffs]
performances.interpretation: Frustrated: someone who feels abandoned and is angry about needing anyone.
performances.direction: Frustrated: someone who feels abandoned and is angry about needing anyone.

scene.before: "It's two days. You're being dramatic about this."
scene.after: "That's not fair and you know it."

performances.input: [warm, a little shy, smiling] I wanted you… to stay.
performances.interpretation: A genuinely affectionate, quiet request.
performances.direction: A genuinely affectionate, quiet request.

scene.before: "I should go. It's really late."

performances.input: [exhausted, overwhelmed, close to tears] I love you. [long exhale] Go away.
performances.interpretation: Exhausted and emotionally overwhelmed.
performances.direction: Exhausted and emotionally overwhelmed.

scene.before: "Talk to me. Please. I'm not leaving until you talk to me."

performances.input: [giggling] I love you. [laughs, pushing him away] Go AWAY.
performances.interpretation: Warmly teasing, with spontaneous laughter.
performances.direction: Adopted from the voice lab (lab-love-b-v4-directed-scene). Laughing at him and at herself.

scene.before: "Say it. Go on. Say it back. I'm not moving till you say it."

performances.input: [angry, jaw tight] I love you. [voice breaking] Go away.
performances.interpretation: Angry, with the hurt showing through underneath.
performances.direction: Angry, with the hurt showing through underneath.

scene.before: "So that's it? You're just going to shut me out again?"

performances.text: I think I was happy then.
performances.input: [surprised, a smile breaking through] I think I was happy then.
performances.interpretation: Nostalgic, with an unexpected smile.
performances.direction: Adopted from the voice lab (lab-happy-a-v4-liam). He did not expect to remember it fondly.

scene.before: "Look at you in this one. How old were you?"

performances.text: I think I was happy then.
performances.input: [uncertain, searching for it] I think… I was happy then?
performances.interpretation: Uncertain, trying to remember.
performances.direction: Uncertain, trying to remember.

scene.before: "Were you happy, back then? In that house?"

performances.text: I think I was happy then.
performances.input: [wistful, very quiet] I think I was happy then… [sighs]
performances.interpretation: Painfully aware of something lost.
performances.direction: Painfully aware of something lost. (First take spoke its tag, "the smile fading", aloud; the direction now lives in the unspoken scene.)

scene.before: He found the photograph in a box he hadn't opened in twenty years. He smiled at it at first. Then the smile went, and he said, very quietly:

performances.input: [laughing] You've got crumbs… [giggles] on you.
performances.interpretation: Genuine happiness; laughing at him, fondly.
performances.direction: Genuine happiness; laughing at him, fondly.

scene.before: "What? Why are you looking at me like that?"

performances.input: [exasperated sigh] Why didn't you UNDERSTAND?
performances.interpretation: Irritation that has been building for a long time.
performances.direction: Irritation that has been building for a long time.

scene.before: "I did what you asked. I don't know what else you want from me."

performances.text: Don't go yet, this bit's good.
performances.input: [affectionate, laughing softly] Don't go yet… this bit's good.
performances.interpretation: Affection: pulling someone back onto the sofa.
performances.direction: Affection: pulling someone back onto the sofa.

scene.before: "I'm going to bed. I can't keep my eyes open."

performances.text: I'm sorry I was like that.
performances.input: [embarrassed, awkward little laugh] I'm sorry I was… like that.
performances.interpretation: Embarrassment: an apology he would rather not have to make.
performances.direction: Embarrassment: an apology he would rather not have to make.

scene.before: "Hey. About last night..."

performances.text: What did you mean by that?
performances.input: [confused, half-laughing] What did you… mean by that?
performances.interpretation: Confusion, not yet sure whether to be hurt.
performances.direction: Confusion, not yet sure whether to be hurt.

scene.before: "Well. Some of us actually finish things."

performances.text: Let me be small for a minute.
performances.input: [tenderly, very quietly] Let me be small… for a minute.
performances.interpretation: Tenderness: asking to be held without explaining why.
performances.direction: Tenderness: asking to be held without explaining why.

scene.before: She put her head on his shoulder and closed her eyes.

performances.input: [grief, voice unsteady] Do you remember me?
performances.interpretation: Grief: a daughter at her mother's bedside.
performances.direction: Grief: a daughter at her mother's bedside.

scene.before: Her mother looked at her for a long time without knowing her. She took her hand anyway.

performances.text: You made me laugh so hard I couldn't breathe.
performances.input: [laughing hard] You made me laugh so hard… [wheezing laugh] I couldn't breathe.
performances.interpretation: Joy, remembered out loud and caught by it again.
performances.direction: Joy, remembered out loud and caught by it again.

scene.before: "Do you remember the thing with the deckchair?"

performances.input: [happily, with a low chuckle] That was a good day.
performances.interpretation: Plain happiness, no ache in it.
performances.direction: Plain happiness, no ache in it.

scene.before: "Remember the beach? You fell asleep in the sun and burnt one side of your face."

performances.input: I wanted you… to stay.
performances.interpretation: Nearly breaking, with the scene doing the work instead of tags.
performances.direction: Lean alternative to stay--breaking (review: stacked tags risk sounding acted). No tags; the unspoken scene carries it.

performances.input: [half-laughing] Do you remember me?

performances.text: If I come closer, will you stay?
